introduction.heading: Plumbing for South Jordan homes
introduction.body:
Half of the homes in South Jordan were built in 2007 or later, and about 9% before 1980, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. In newer homes like these, the first big plumbing jobs are often water heaters, fixtures and water softeners as the original equipment ages. A water heater usually lasts 10 to 15 years.

South Jordan buys all of its drinking water from the Jordan Valley Water Conservancy District, which draws on Deer Creek and Jordanelle reservoirs, the Provo River and some groundwater. Hardness is 7 to 10 grains per gallon, according to the city's water page, which labels it hard. The U.S. Geological Survey classes that as moderately hard to hard water. Hard water leaves mineral deposits in water heaters, faucets and appliances, and a water softener or filtration system cuts that buildup.

South Jordan supplies secondary canal water to part of the city, and says it will audit backflow devices on properties with secondary water access.
